newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee down as state-run bank buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee down as state-run bank buys dollars.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened to 35.80/81 per dollar on sustained demand for the U.S. currency in active trade on Thursday, dealers said.
"The movement was one-way," a dealer at a foreign bank said. "The rupee opened down from yesterday's levels and fell further on dollar buying from a state-run bank," he said.
The Reserve Bank of India bought dollars at 35.80 rupee levels, a dealer said.
Premia on forward dollars climbed on profit-taking, dealers said. The premia for six-month dollars ended Thursday at 10.35 percent against Wednesday's close of 10.15 percent, they said.
